observation.visible_scene: Close-up of a candlelit table: two hands, one emerging from a white cuff (foreground) and one from a dark blue suit sleeve (right), each holding a stemmed glass of pale white wine. The two glasses are tilted toward one another with their bowls overlapping/touching in a toast-like pose. On the table are a lit white taper candle in a glass holder at left, a folded white napkin, a red rose, and a cluster of green grapes at lower right, against a blurred brown background. A faint 'PREVIEW' watermark overlays the center.
visible_changes: The pair of glasses drifts slowly to the right and slightly upward within the frame over the excerpt, while staying together in the overlapping toast position.
Relative to the background objects (candle, grapes, napkin), the glasses translate rightward, indicating the hands/glasses move in scene space in addition to the framing shift.
The background (candle, rose, grapes, wall) also shifts rightward across the frame edges, consistent with a slow camera pan/framing drift rather than motion of the table items themselves.
The wine surfaces and the reflections/refractions through the glass bowls change subtly as the glasses tilt and move, with small sloshing of the liquid line.
The candle flame flickers and changes shape slightly frame to frame.

The overlap geometry of the two bowls changes: early frames show the foreground bowl left of the background bowl; later frames show the foreground bowl shifted right, more centered over the background bowl.
outside_clip_unknowns: Whether a clink/contact event occurred before the segment start or a drink follows after the segment end (both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries).
The identities, faces, or full bodies of the two people.
The full table setting and room beyond the blurred background.
uncertain_details: Exact split between hand motion and camera pan is approximate; both contribute to the rightward drift.
Whether the glass rims/bowls remain in continuous contact or separate and re-contact slightly is not fully resolvable from the sampled frames.
The precise cause of the liquid's small surface changes (motion vs. reflection shift) is not distinguishable.
